claims.statement: The GHEC-only fragment prohibits EMU members from forking outside-enterprise repositories or internal repositories. Its categorical internal-fork prohibition conflicts with the same pinned source's emu-forks.md allowance for internal enterprise repositories as enterprise policy permits, reviewed in tranche 214. The contradiction remains unresolved; neither statement is adopted or silently treated as a version override, and no fork behavior was tested.

The GHEC branch prohibits EMU members from creating gists and describes read-only gist access. This does not establish access to every private gist, anonymous access or actual enforcement; no gist was created or modified.

The GHEC branch limits EMU repository interaction to repositories within the enterprise. The fragment does not define every interaction or establish repository membership and permissions; it is not a claim that all outside public content is unreadable.

The GHEC branch limits EMU proposals to enterprise repositories. Proposal scope is not entitlement to merge, write or bypass review within the enterprise, and no changes were proposed through this source review.

The GHEC branch limits EMU repository changes to enterprise repositories. Enterprise inclusion is a necessary scope boundary, not sufficient write permission, universal access or protection bypass; no permissions or repositories were changed.

The source strongly recommends storing setup-user credentials in the company's password-management tool, because that user is needed for authentication updates, IdP or protocol migration and enterprise recovery-code use. This is an upstream recommendation, not an adopted credential control or actual encrypted custody, access or recovery receipt. No credential was read, copied or stored.
